turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, Mr.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Whittaker.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm Megan Kowalczyk, the nurse practitioner in the Heart Failure Clinic. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Darnell Whittaker, February 27, 1958

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you. The nurse said you called on Monday about some swelling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What's been happening? Yeah, my ankles have been puffing up for about a week. My shoes are tight by the afternoon and the scale says I'm up seven pounds. Okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: what's your usual weight at home?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm usually right around 182. This morning it was 189.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And how's your breathing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Worse than usual, normally I can walk three blocks to the corner store. Now I'm winded after about one block.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How many pillows are you sleeping on? I've gone from one pillow to two,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: feels easier to breathe propped up. Are you waking up at night,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: gasping for air?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No not that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any chest pain, or feeling like you might pass out?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No chest pain, no passing out.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything different with your diet, the last couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well my nephew got married two weekends ago, there was a lot of ham, a lot of salty food, Dude, I wasn't careful, I'll admit it. My wife Lorraine already gave me an earful. That happens.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's go through your medicines. You're on sacubitral Valsartan. 49 and 51 milligrams twice a day. Carvedilol 12 .5 milligrams twice a day. Spironolactone 25 milligrams once a and Dapagliff lives in 10 milligrams once a day. Still taking all of those.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every one of them, Lorraine fills my pill box on Sundays.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And the furor smite, how much are you taking?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The water pill is 20 milligrams in the morning. Wait, no, it's the 40.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: They changed it in the summer, it's 40.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 40 milligrams once a day is what I have. Anything over the counter.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Um, I've been taking naproxen for my knees. The arthritis acts up. Two of the 220 milligram pills twice a day for about two weeks.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, that's important. I'll come back to that. Let me check you over. Your weight here is 189 pounds. Blood pressure is 112 over 70, pulse 78, and oxygen is 95 percent on room air, your neck veins are up to about 10 centimeters. I hear some crackles at the bottom of both lungs. Heart is regular, and I hear a soft extra sound called an S3, and you've got two -plus pitting swelling up to the middle of both shins.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That doesn't sound great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It tells me you're holding onto extra fluid. Your last echo in March showed an ejection fraction of 30 percent, so your heart pump is weaker than normal and it's sensitive to salt. Your labs from three weeks ago were okay, potassium 4, 6, and creatinine 1 .2.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So what do we do?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So this is a mild flare of your heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. I think the salty food and the naproxen both played a part. Naproxen makes the kidneys hold onto salt and water. So I want you to stop it completely.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What do I take for the knees then?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Acetaminophen is safer for your heart. You can take 650 milligrams, up to three times a day. For the fluid, I'm increasing the furosamide to 40 milligrams twice a day. for the next five days. Once your weight is back near 183, go back to 40 milligrams once a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, 40 twice a day for five days. Right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep all your other heart medicines the same. Weigh yourself every morning after you use the bathroom and write it down. Keep salt under 2 ,000 milligrams a day and fluids to about two liters.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Lorraine's going to love that she's been on me about the salt.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'd also like a basic metabolic panel on the 21st of October to make sure your kidneys and potassium are okay with a higher dose. Call us if your weight goes up three pounds in a day or five pounds in a week. If you're short of breath at rest or you get chest pain go to the emergency room.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Got it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And are you using the patient portal? I can send you the instructions there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, it's Darnell .Wittaker at ExampleyMail .com.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect. I'll send the plan there, and I want to see you back in one week to check your weight and the swelling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good. Thank you, Megan.
